title: Customer-tier qcache + batching revenue model (draft)
content:
Context:
This is a working draft to align batching, qcache TTLs, and quantization allowances per customer tier and to produce a small spreadsheet model that ties those settings to expected cost per 1M tokens and revenue uplift opportunities. Goal is to produce a single-pane spreadsheet that sales/solutions can use to justify Dedicated commitments and for Product to bake sensible defaults into Optimize presets.

High-level objective:
- Define conservative, middling, and aggressive settings for qcache TTL, batch size targets, and allowed quant profiles by tier (Free, Growth, Business, Enterprise)
- Provide a small, auditable spreadsheet model (columns/formulas below) that outputs: estimated infra cost per 1M tokens, expected 95th tail latency, recommended default preset, and revenue delta if we convert X% of customers to Dedicated or higher tiers.

Assumptions (callouts):
- Baseline model: open-llama-13B-ish (serving profile median token cost ~0.0009 $/token on hosted with current qconfig) — replace with actual benchmark numbers when available
- Avg prompt length (input + reference) differs by product archetype; spreadsheet will accept per-cohort override
- qcache hit reduces per-token cost by ~35% for typical prefix-heavy chat flows (empirical; depends heavily on prompt reuse)
- Batch efficiency improves token throughput but increases mean latency by ~5-25% depending on size and request arrival pattern
- Quantization: FP16 (baseline), INT8, 4-bit (GPTQ/LLM-specific) — quality regressions measured separately; pricing benefits assumed 1.35x cost improvement for int8, 1.8x for 4-bit on compatible kernels

Tier definitions and recommended defaults (first-pass):
- Free / Trial:
  - qcache TTL: 30s
  - batching: opportunistic only; max batch window 10ms; target batch size 4
  - quantization allowed: FP16 only
  - notes: prioritize latency; strict tail SLO 300ms for 90% requests

- Growth (self-serve paying):
  - qcache TTL: 2min for conversational routes, 30s for stateless generation
  - batching: small-window batching; max batch delay 25ms; target batch size 8-12 depending on arrival rate
  - quantization allowed: FP16 + optional INT8 for 'cost-first' routes (customer opt-in)
  - notes: balanced latency/cost; provide Optimize preset 'growth-balanced'

- Business (committed monthly):
  - qcache TTL: 5min convo / 1min stateless by default
  - batching: adaptive: allow larger batches when throughput > X rps (configurable); target 16 at steady state
  - quantization allowed: FP16 + INT8 recommended; 4-bit evaluable per workload
  - notes: recommend canary of INT8 at 5% of traffic for quality guardrails; tailoring via Optimize suggestions

- Enterprise (SLA + Dedicated/Private):
  - qcache TTL: customer-configurable; default 15min for session-heavy apps
  - batching: aggressive batching allowed (window up to 100ms) for throughput-critical routes; strong per-route SLO overrides
  - quantization allowed: customer choice; Enable INT8 by default on compute-optimized stacks; 4-bit for cost-first non-critical pipelines
  - notes: tradeoffs exposed in Console; sales can accept higher latency for cost savings if customer signs Dedicated commit

Spreadsheet: required columns and formulas (single-sheet minimal model)
Columns (inputs):
- Tier (dropdown)
- Monthly RPS (requests per second)
- Avg tokens per request (tokens_in + tokens_out)
- Prompt reuse factor (0..1) — fraction of tokens served from qcache
- Target tail SLO (ms)
- Allowed quant profile (FP16 / INT8 / 4bit)
- Batch target size (numeric) — if blank, model picks default by tier
- qcache TTL (secs) — if blank, model picks default by tier
- GPU cost per hour (USD) — regional override
- Overhead multiplier (for networking, infra) default 1.12

Derived columns / formulas (Excel-friendly):
- Effective tokens per request = Avg tokens per request * (1 - Prompt reuse factor)
- Tokens per second (TPS) = Monthly RPS * Effective tokens per request / 1 (adjust units consistent)
- Hourly token throughput = TPS * 3600
- GPU throughput (tokens/hour per GPU) = baseline_throughput_by_quant_profile (sheet param) * batch efficiency factor(batch size)
- Required GPUs = CEILING( Hourly token throughput / (GPU throughput * utilization_factor) ) ; utilization_factor default 0.8
- Hourly infra cost = Required GPUs * GPU cost per hour * Overhead multiplier
- Cost per token = Hourly infra cost / Hourly token throughput
- Cost per 1M tokens = Cost per token * 1,000,000
- Expected mean latency = base_latency_by_model + batching_latency_penalty(batch size) - qcache_latency_savings(prompt reuse factor) 
  (express as ms; keep simple lookup tables or piecewise linear approximations in sheet)
- 95th latency estimate = Expected mean latency * tail_multiplier_by_tier (eg 1.8 for Free, 1.4 for Enterprise)
- Revenue per 1M tokens (tiered pricing param) = user_input; Revenue delta = Revenue - Cost per 1M tokens

Example row (illustrative numbers — replace with real bench):
- Tier: Growth
- Monthly RPS: 50
- Avg tokens/request: 150
- Prompt reuse: 0.25
- Allowed quant: INT8
- Derived: Effective tokens/request = 112.5 -> Hourly tokens = 50*112.5*3600 = 20,250,000 tokens/hr -> Required GPUs = 3 (example) -> Hourly infra cost = $36/hr -> Cost per 1M tokens = ~$1.78 (example)
- Notes: shows conversion from hosted $/token baseline to Dedicated-like numbers when batching and INT8 applied

Sensitivity knobs to expose in the sheet UI:
- Prompt reuse range slider (0–0.9) with live delta to cost per 1M tokens
- Batch window slider (0–200ms) affecting batch size and latency penalty
- Quantization toggle with assumed speedups (editable)
- Canary percent for quantization quality guardrail (simulate cost/latency mixing)

Quality and safety guardrails (operational notes):
- Always recommend running quality evals (automated prompt suites) before enabling INT8/4-bit at >10% of traffic
- Provide an automatic rollback trigger if evaluation metrics fall by >X% or if human review flags regressions
- For session-heavy apps, prefer longer qcache TTL only after ensuring privacy/data retention settings are compatible

Sales/Revenue tie-ins (how sales can use this):
- Generate a one-pager from the spreadsheet for customer: show current hosted cost estimate vs expected committed-cost with recommended preset
- Provide a simple sensitivity table: "if prompt_reuse >= 0.4 and we enable INT8 + batching, you save ~Y% on token spend"
- Attach a short checklist for Solutions Engineers to validate before recommending aggressive quantization to customers (eval run id, SLA agreement, fallback route configured)

Open questions and action items (for next sync):
- A1: Get canonical baseline throughput numbers per-model/per-quant from Serving team (Marco)
- A2: Confirm quality multipliers for INT8/4-bit (Sofia to run small eval suite)
- A3: Add region-specific GPU $/hour values and validate overhead multiplier with Infra (Jonas)
- A4: Build first-pass spreadsheet in Google Sheets and add to Optimize templates; run 10 customer samples to sanity-check outputs (Owner: Asha)

Notes to self / messy thoughts (leave in doc):
- Might want to include a small chart that shows cost vs latency frontier for each tier — but keep the first sheet simple
- Consider adding a 'recommended default preset' generator that outputs JSON for Console ingestion (mapping tier -> qcache/batch/quant profile)
- Keep canary workflow simple: start at 5% traffic with performance tracing and auto rollback on stderr/anomaly

Next steps (short timeline):
- Week 1: collect benchmark numbers, finalize param table for sheet
- Week 2: build sheet + examples, circulate to Product + Solutions
- Week 3: iterate with Sales on one-pager and where to expose in Console

If you read this and want to change any of the first-pass defaults, highlight in comments — trying to lock a pragmatic set to test on 3 customer pilots.

-- Asha
